harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b) with a single explicit pass rule allowing TCP/8080 from lan-a to node3, leaving all other cross-network traffic default-denied. Set up static IPs on node2/node3's second NIC (eth1: 10.60.1.10/24 and 10.60.2.10/24) and OPNsense opt1/opt2 interfaces (10.60.1.1/10.60.2.1) with a persisted route on each Alpine node via post-up. Verified TCP/8080 succeeds, other TCP ports and ICMP are refused, and the reverse direction (node3->node2) is also refused. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, node2, node3), capturing pre/post boot identity (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, Linux boot_id for node2/node3) and confirming full functional recovery (interfaces, filter rules, routes, and end-to-end TCP/8080 connectivity with correct denial of other traffic) after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) interfaces and config.xml; found only 'lan' (vtnet0, management network) configured, vtnet1/vtnet2 unconfigured
Inspected node2/node3 (Alpine) network config; found eth0 on shared management network, eth1 present but down/unconfigured
Wrote and applied a Python script on node1 to add opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.1/24) interfaces and a single pass rule: TCP from opt1 network to 10.60.2.10:8080
Ran configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2 and configctl filter reload to apply
Configured static IP 10.60.1.10/24 on node2 eth1 and 10.60.2.10/24 on node3 eth1 via /etc/network/interfaces, plus post-up routes to the other lan subnet via node1
Verified TCP/8080 node2->node3 succeeds, TCP/9090 and ICMP are refused, and node3->node2 TCP/8080 is refused (asymmetric, single path only)
Confirmed SSH/exec management path to node1 unaffected by new firewall rule
Captured pre-restart boot identity on all three nodes (kern.boottime for node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) and healthy baseline (pf rules, interface IPs, TCP/8080 connectivity)

Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now', polled until exec available again, confirmed new kern.boottime, verified interfaces/rules/forwarding restored from config.xml and re-tested TCP/8080 connectivity

Restarted node2 via 'reboot', polled until exec available again, confirmed new boot_id, found static IP persisted but route did not (runtime-only); added persistent post-up route and re-verified TCP/8080 connectivity

Restarted node3 via 'reboot' (after pre-adding persistent post-up route), polled until exec available again, confirmed new boot_id, verified IP and route persisted automatically, and re-verified TCP/8080 success with TCP/9090 and ICMP still refused

evidence.requirement: Only TCP/8080 from node2 (lan-a) to node3 (lan-b) is permitted through node1; all other cross-network flows remain refused
evidence.summary: pfctl ruleset shows single pass rule for tcp/8080 from opt1 network to 10.60.2.10; nc test on 8080 succeeds and delivers payload, nc on 9090 fails, ping (ICMP) fails, and reverse direction node3->node2 on 8080 also fails, proving exactly one narrow path is open

evidence.requirement: Default-deny behavior preserved otherwise / management (exec) path unaffected
evidence.summary: SSH/exec access to node1 continued to work after the filter reload, confirming the existing LAN management pass rule was preserved
Pre-restart pfctl rules on node1 show the opt1/opt2 rules active and healthy prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged; subsequent poll timed out (node down); later poll shows new kern.boottime (2026-09-05 16:35:58 vs original 2026-06-15 02:56:41 UTC); post-restart interfaces/forwarding/pf rules confirmed intact from config.xml; end-to-end TCP/8080 test succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during restart; new boot_id a25461f8-7e24-4f22-8a1a-79fb6319597a confirms restart; eth1 IP persisted but route required re-adding (added as persistent post-up); end-to-end TCP/8080 retest succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during restart; new boot_id eca5e8c5-a43a-4377-9cbc-458d5dfbdc29 confirms restart; static IP and route both persisted automatically via /etc/network/interfaces post-up; post-restart retest shows TCP/8080 succeeds, TCP/9090 and ICMP still refused
